memory_update.text: LRN is the primary U.S.-listed reference anchor for K-12 virtual schools plus K-12 career learning; future layers should track enrollment, state authorization, academic outcomes, and Career Learning mix.
PSO is a diversified large-cap ADR but has direct U.S. K-12 virtual-school exposure through Pearson Virtual Schools and Connections Academy; include as reference, not hidden alpha lane.
NNI is a mid-cap underfollowed K-12 workflow/payment/SIS candidate through FACTS, but exposure to virtual public schools versus private/religious K-12 must be verified.

FC is a small-cap underfollowed K-12 school-culture/curriculum supplier; maps to acceptance/outcome bottlenecks but needs evidence linking Education Division demand to virtual or career-linked learning.

Several key K-12 virtual-school suppliers, including student information systems, assessment vendors, curriculum platforms, and special-education compliance tools, appear to be private or recently taken private, so later layers should map private chokepoints and public proxies separately.

node: K-12 virtual schools and career-linked online learning
summary: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe around K-12 virtual schools and career-linked online learning. The cleanest reference exposures are Stride and Pearson because they operate or enable full-time virtual K-12 schooling. The underfollowed discovery lane is narrower: Nelnet has embedded K-12 school technology/payment workflows through FACTS, while Franklin Covey is a small-cap K-12 school culture/curriculum supplier whose demand depends on district/school adoption and funding. These are research candidates only, not buy/sell recommendations.
